That neoliberal grip on policy has waned, and on the left, we’re happy to see it—you love to see it in certain respects—but they were the most powerful constituency against this whole rivalry impulse the whole time. You see a little bit of China’s assertiveness on the military side starting in 2007, but really started in about 2008-2009. It’s not because they’re communist. China is neoliberalism’s greatest success story if we’re being clear eyed; they’re hyper-capitalist. It’s not a clash of civilizations because it’s the same civilization before and since 2008. It’s not that Xi Jinping is evil, even though he might be—he’s a tyrant. But Xi Jinping didn’t come to power until 2012-2013, and the aggressiveness started ramping up in 2007-2008.

So, a little bit of this is the product of the military-industrial complex, and much of it is the global financial crisis, which again, was brought on by us and fed perceptions in China of the decline of American authority and legitimacy.
